function.name: client_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates of a single client based on the client's name and the status of the mandate. Partners can use this API to retrieve mandate information for their clients. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the client whose mandates are to be fetched.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If not specified, mandates with all statuses are retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches all mandates for all clients associated with a partner, filtered by the status of the mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of mandates to fetch. Possible values are 'active', 'pending', and 'inactive'.

function.name: partner_sips
function.description: Fetch all Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs) of all clients associated with a partner, filtered by the given status of the SIP. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the SIPs to be fetched. Valid statuses include 'active', 'stopped', and 'paused'.

message.content:
A **mandate** in financial services refers to an official authorization or instruction issued by a client (or investor) to a service provider—such as a bank, investment firm, or fintech platform—to act on behalf of the client in managing certain assets or executing specific transactions. Key points about a mandate: | Aspect | Description | |--------|-------------| | **Purpose** | Grants permission for the service provider to manage funds, execute trades, or perform other fiduciary duties under agreed terms. | | **Types** | • *Active* – Currently valid and enforceable.
• *Pending* – Awaiting approval or completion of formalities.
• *Inactive/Expired* – No longer valid; may have been revoked or reached its end date. | | **Scope** | Can cover various asset classes such as equities, bonds, mutual funds, systematic investment plans (SIP), etc., depending on the agreement. | | **Legal Basis** | Often governed by regulatory frameworks like SEBI’s Mutual Fund Mandate Regulations in India, which set out how mandates must be documented, disclosed, and monitored. | | **Benefits** | • Enables automated portfolio management.
• Provides transparency through regular reporting.
• Allows investors to delegate day‑to‑day decisions while retaining ultimate control over strategy. | In practice, when you see “client mandates” or “partner mandates,” it usually means retrieving records of those authorizations from your system—for example, using APIs to list all active mandates for a particular client or all pending ones across partners.
